main_body: Multi-storey office/school block drawn as a straight front elevation: a flat rooftop plane at the top (rows 1-37) over a windowed facade with four floors of windows and an entrance door.
top_band: Rows 1-2 light lavender #e3dff2 are only the roof parapet edge; rows 7-37 are a roof deck of L~168/147, which is a rooftop plan painted face-on with AC units, not a receding top over the facade. No clearly distinct top band separated from the front face by a step.
evidence: The facade is a flat front elevation: windows, floor bands and the door are painted flat on one plane. The upper 'roof' area is drawn as a rectangular plan view of a flat rooftop (AC units, skylight) stacked directly above the facade with only a 1-row green line and a light edge between them. That does not make a foreshortened top over a front face; it is the roof seen top-down next to the elevation, and the parapet is a 1-2 row rim. Windows are flat-painted with no inset reveal, and there is no eave shadow. By the strict rule this is a front elevation with a hat and it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 4 lightness steps on its concrete ramp (highlight, light, mid, dark), plus speckle texture on the walls and glass diagonals on the windows. The outline is tinted (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so it is not a sticker look. Its 9 colours per tile is near the stone reference (11) but well below the tile reference (18), and 32 distinct colours is far fewer than the references' 66 and 185. Flat-fill coverage is low (9%). The repeating window grid is mechanical, and the surfaces are less rich than the references (no per-unit shading), so it reads thinner than the Beodeul pieces. It does not clearly match the standard.
